content.overview: BNS s. 58 — Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. BNS restatement of IPC 118. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 118. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 58 is the rule on “Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life”. The section provides that whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals by any act or omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 58 exists so that “Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
58. Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals by any act or omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–

(a) if that offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years; or

(b) if the offence be not committed, with imprisonment of either description, for a term which may extend to three years,

and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals by any act or omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–
2. (a) if that offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years; or
3. (b) if the offence be not committed, with imprisonment of either description, for a term which may extend to three years,
4. and shall also be liable to fine

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, knowing that dacoity is about to be committed at B, falsely informs the Magistrate that a dacoity is about to be committed at C, a place in an opposite direction, and thereby misleads the Magistrate with intent to facilitate the commission of the offence. The dacoity is committed at B in pursuance of the design. A is punishable under this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 58 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 58 (Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life), Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals by any act or omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–

learningObjectives: Understand the offence of concealing capital/life crime designs under BNS s. 58.
Analyze the active facilitation through concealment, false representation, or omission.
Examine the two sentencing tiers: offence committed (up to 7 years) vs offence not committed (up to 3 years).
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 58 provides that whoever, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design, shall, if that offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or, if the offence be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years; and in either case shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Active concealment or false representation designed to shield a capital conspiracy from detection creates independent criminal liability, as it directly aids the perpetration of grave atrocities.
statutoryFramework: Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt, BNS s. 58 (corresponding to IPC s. 118, updated with modern digital concealment).
Mental element: Intending to facilitate or knowing likely to facilitate.
Concealment methods: Act, illegal omission, encryption/information hiding tools, or false representation.
Penalty Tier 1 (Offence committed): Imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
Penalty Tier 2 (Offence not committed): Imprisonment up to three years and fine.
essentialIngredients: There was a design to commit an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment.
The accused voluntarily concealed the design (by act, illegal omission, encryption/hiding tools, or false statements).
The accused acted intending or knowing he would thereby facilitate the commission.
Offence committed = up to 7 years; Offence not committed = up to 3 years.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 58 criminalizes the deliberate sheltering of capital plots. Crucially, the BNS modernizes the text by explicitly including 'the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool' to conceal a design to commit murder or treason. If an accomplice knows that a terrorist plot or assassination is underway, and deliberately misleads investigating agencies or uses encrypted dead-drops to hide weapons blueprints, he is punished under s. 58. The penalty is seven years if the plot succeeds, and three years if law enforcement foils it.
examples: Teaching example (False representation): A knows that dacoits are about to attack a village warehouse and kill the guards. When the police inspector asks A where the armed gang went, A deliberately points in the opposite direction. A is liable under s. 58.

Teaching example (Encrypted hiding): An operative uses specialized steganography tools to conceal assassination blueprints inside innocent image files to facilitate a murder conspiracy. Section 58 directly applies.
distinctions: Concealing capital design (s. 58) vs Ordinary imprisonment design (s. 60): Section 58 applies to capital/life crimes (7/3 years); Section 60 applies to lesser offences (1/4th or 1/8th fraction).
Mere silence vs Voluntary concealment: Mere failure of an ordinary citizen to report is not an offence unless an illegal omission or active false representation exists.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an individual who used steganographic tools to hide maps of a planned terrorist assault on a military base is liable under BNS s. 58.
Rule: Section 58 explicitly penalizes voluntary concealment by encryption or information hiding tools intending to facilitate an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment.
Application: The planned offence (waging war) is capital, and encryption tools were deliberately deployed to hide the plot.
Conclusion: The individual is guilty under s. 58.
